item.text: {"text":"For one target, let N include the target plus all eligible catalog competitors after filtering; let r be its 1-based rank under a fixed total ordering. Sampling m distinct competitors uniformly without replacement gives X ~ Hypergeom(N−1, r−1, m), where sampled rank = X+1. Thus expected sampled HR@10 = P(X≤9) = Σ[x=0…9] C(r−1,x)C(N−r,m−x)/C(N−1,m), treating infeasible terms as zero; compute with scipy.stats.hypergeom.cdf(9,N−1,r−1,m). Here m=99 means 100 total candidates. Average probabilities over users, then equally over categories. This is a direct application of the [hypergeometric distribution](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy-1.14.0/reference/generated/scipy.stats.hypergeom.html). Smaller candidate sets mechanically increase hit probability; sampled metrics can even reverse model comparisons ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).\n\nRecommended comparison controls: identical users, targets, eligible pools, filtering rules, and final unique candidate counts across uniform, popularity-weighted, and lexical sets. Exclude the target from negative sampling and insert it exactly once; remove only authorized, observed known-positive conflicts before selection, deduplicate, and refill from the corresponding eligible sampler. Report removals, shortages, and actual counts; never consult hidden labels. Recompute r on the filtered universe. Use the evaluator’s tie policy consistently: fixed item-ID tie-breaking defines r; randomized ties require averaging tie outcomes rather than counting only strictly higher scores. Fix candidate sets across models and repeat diagnostic sampling to quantify uncertainty. Popularity and lexical selection change competitor difficulty, so full rank alone cannot predict their HR using the ordinary hypergeometric law; compare against count-matched uniform controls. These controls are methodological recommendations, consistent with documented [sampling-strategy sensitivity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045), and should leave the pinned evaluator unchanged."}
